full_judgment:
10. Section 4 of the AM has established the Artha Rin Adalat, while section 5(1) confers exclusive jurisdiction upon Artha Rin Adalat to hear all suits for recovery of loan of the financing institutions, Sub-section (I) of Section 5 of the AM reads as follows: ৫। (১) অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৫) ও (৬) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ঋণ আদায় সম্পর্কিত যাবতীয় মামলা ধারা ৪ এর অধীন প্রতিষ্ঠিত, ঘোষিত বা গণ্য হওয়া অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে দায়ের করিতে হইবে এবং উক্ত আদালতেই উহাদের নিষ্পত্তি হইবে, while sub-section 11 of Section 5 reads as follows-" (১১) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত একটি দেওয়ানী আদালত হিসাবে গণ্যও হইবে এবং এই আইনের বিধানাবলীর সহিত অসংগতিপূর্ণ না হওয়া সাপেক্ষে, দেওয়ানী আদালতের সমস্ত ক্ষমতা ও এখতিয়ার উহার থাকিবে।” Sub-section (11) of section 5 of the AM, provides that the Artha Rin Adalat shall be deem to be a Civil Court and that the Adalat shall have all the powers and jurisdiction of the Civil Court, unless any provision of the Civil Procedure Code inconsistent with any provisions of the AM. Chapter 6 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 contains section 26 to Section 39. This chapter deals with procedure for execution of the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 12. Having examined the provisions of Ain, we find that the Adalat is deem to be a Civil Court, as it stipulated in section 5(11) of the Ain, whereas section 5(1) stipulates that all suit for recovery of money of the financing institutions shall by filed before the Adalat. On the other hand sub-section (5) of section 33 of the Ain, empowers the Adalat to issue certificate of possession of the mortgaged property, to the decree-holder bank, so that the beak can take step to sell the mortgaged property and can hand over the possession of the sold property to the buyer. Whereas, subsection (7) of section 33 further enables the Adalat to issue certificate, conferring title of the mortgaged property in favour of the decree holder bank. Under section 34 of the Ain, Adalat can pass order of civil imprisonment against the judgment-debtor. But the court entertaining an application under section 138 (1) of the N.I. Act and disposing of the case filed under the said section, is neither a Civil Court, nor it has any power or jurisdiction to entertain any suit for recovery of money due to a bank or financing, institutions or any application for execution of a decree. 

 13. A case under section 5 of the Ain is filed for recovery of money, through the execution process is laid down under chapter VI of the Ain. On the other hand, a case under section 138 (1) of the N.I. Act,1881, is filed seeking punishment of a person alleged to have committed offence under section 138 (1) of the N.I. Act. If the drawer of the cheque is found guilty of committing the offence under section 138 (1) of the N.I. Act, then he/she is to be sentenced as a convict, not as a judgment debtor. Hence, in our considered opinion that a civil suit or a suit filed under the Ain, 2003, for recovery of money and a complaint filed under section 138(1) of the N.I. Act, 1881, are quite two different proceedings, filed in two different forums, seeking two different reliefs. The proceeding initiated under section 138(1) of the N.I. Act, 1881 is not filed for recovery of money, but for securing punishment under that section. An order imposing fine under section 138 (1) of the N.I. Act is not and cannot be treated as a decree for recovery of money, which is within the; province or Civil Court or Adalat.
